Hi Samantha / Marissa / team — Neha from Redwood Security here. Thanks for the clear list — below are concise answers and what we can share today. I’ve attached the SOC 2 report and a short technical note on retention/delete behavior.

- SOC 2: We are SOC 2 Type II certified; attached file is the 2026 report redacted for customer sharing (SOC2_Report_2026.pdf). Full report available under NDA.
- HIPAA / BAA: Redwood supports HIPAA-covered workloads via our Private deployment and BAA. For Hosted customers processing PHI we require a signed BAA; we can provide a BAA addendum and place consenting customers on our Private or Dedicated offerings per their compliance needs.
- Retention windows (configurable):
  - Inference request payloads: configurable retention 0–90 days (default 30 days).
  - Request metadata & logs: default 90 days, configurable down to 7 days for critical audit logs.
  - KV cache/prefix cache: ephemeral by default tied to model/session lifecycle; customers can opt-in to longer retention for telemetry.
- Deletion / backups:
  - Backups/snapshots: periodic backups do include metadata and operational logs; we do not persist raw request/response payloads in long-term backup snapshots by default. For Dedicated/Private customers we can configure backup policies to exclude request/response payloads.
  - Deletion propagation: For Hosted customers, deletion requests will remove primary copies within the configured SLA window (e.g., 30 days). Backups are on a rolling snapshot lifecycle; when a deletion is requested we mark records for purge on next snapshot compaction and ensure cryptographic shredding is scheduled within 30–60 days depending on retention tier. For Dedicated/Private customers we can contractually shorten that window.

Estimated questionnaire turnaround: 3–5 business days for the standard XLS questionnaire; quicker (1–2 days) if you prefer a short call and a prioritized Q/A set.

Attachments:
- SOC2_Report_2026.pdf
- Data_Retention_Delete_SLA_Note.pdf
